content.text: The introduced equals was for a private class with no fields. I've removed it in the following PR (to get your feedback). It's possible that Sonar would now give a different warning ("missing equals" or something). But  this is one of the cases, I think, where Sonar rule (not sure which one) should be disabled.

Also, just to clarify, it doesn't seem to me that VersionsRdfContext.equals() was disabled in the commit you mentioned. Could you point to the line if you did mean VersionsRdfContext and not the private  Versions2Triples class?

L126 equals was added to the private class to quell a Sonar warning, so there was no VersionsRdfContext.equals(), as the issue description seems to suggest – unless I'm not seeing it. I've removed the introduced equals() the subsequent PR.
Added a minor javadoc change to the PR.
It is most likely not a good idea to disable VersionsRdfContext.equals(). Instead, a proper equals() method should exist that with a hashCode() method that abides by the contract:
